content.title: About
content.content: The chocolate croissant is a French pastry consisting of a buttery, flaky dough rolled into a crescent shape and filled with dark chocolate. Its crisp outer layer and melt‑in‑your‑mouth interior make it a popular breakfast item and snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Croissants originated in Austria in the 17th century and were later refined by French bakers.
In France the chocolate version is called “pain au chocolat.”
Traditional fillings use dark chocolate with at least 70 % cocoa content.
The flaky texture comes from repeatedly folding butter into the dough, creating over 100 layers after baking.
In some countries the pastry is dusted with powdered sugar or chopped nuts before serving.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: The combination of carbohydrates from the dough and fats from butter and chocolate provides a quick energy boost.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Dark chocolate is rich in flavonoids that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Rich in magnesium
items.content: Magnesium in chocolate supports muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Provides iron
items.content: Cocoa contributes iron, which helps maintain healthy hemoglobin levels.

items.title: Mood enhancer
items.content: Chocolate stimulates serotonin production, which can improve mood.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Chocolate croissants are calorie‑dense; moderation is important for weight management.

items.title: Sugar and saturated fat
items.content: The amount of sugar and butter can negatively affect cholesterol levels if consumed in excess.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The dough contains wheat, making it unsuitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Cocoa allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chocolate.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Chocolate croissants are best enjoyed warm, straight from the oven. Eat them as a snack, pair with coffee, milk, or fruit yogurt. For a lighter taste, lightly dust with powdered sugar.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store croissants in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. For longer storage keep them refrigerated (up to 5 days) or frozen (up to 1 month). Reheat in the oven for 5‑7 minutes before serving to restore crispness.
